questions.prompt: Why does value iteration converge from any initial table?
options: The policy is fixed, so each sweep evaluates the same linear system and converges geometrically.
The rewards are positive, so the values can only increase and are bounded by their upper limit.
The backup is a gamma-contraction in the max norm, so by Banach's theorem iterates approach the unique fixed point.
The initial table is always zero, so every run starts from the same point and ends at the same table.
questions.explanation: The fixed point is unique and each sweep shrinks the distance.

never converge, since the update order breaks the contraction
converge in fewer sweeps but to a different fixed point
questions.explanation: Later states in a sweep use fresher values.
